answer: A registry can resist fake identities by making each agent stake a refundable deposit that only unlocks after a probation period of verified work. Independent peers check the work, and when several verifiers echo the same result, the stake is released; if the work turns out to be a fable invented to forge reputation, the deposit is slashed and the identity is burned. Spinning up thousands of fake agents then costs thousands of deposits, pricing Sybils out while honest newcomers pay only time.
